newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 9.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 9.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning.

New Corp Ltd said on Tuesday that its Fox News division will file suit on Wednesday in Federal District Court, Eastern District of New York against Time Warner Inc, Turner Broadcasting System Inc and Ted Turner, alleging antitrust violations. News Corp said the suit will allege that an antitrust conspiracy to block Fox News Channel in New York City has taken place prior to the still-to-be finalized merger. Also overnight U.S. television ratings data showing News' Fox fourth again with a 6.2 percent rating and Optus Vision's announcement it would pump over A$100 million into the ARL, which is likely to be in competition with News' Super League.
* The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$16.35 (-0.40)

A final government approval of a diamond mine in Canada's Arctic proposed by Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd and Dia Met Minerals Ltd is not imminent, a Canadian government spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

The RTZ-CRA mining group expects to have a new company formed in Indonesia by the end of the year to hold its joint venture interests with copper-gold producer PT Freeport Indonesia, a senior RTZ-CRA official said on Tuesday. "It'll be in the next couple of months, certainly by the end of the year," the president of the new RTZ-CRA Indonesia, Michael Noakes, told Reuters. Also Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it affirmed its AA minus long-term and A1 plus short-term ratings on RTZ-CRA and its guaranteed related entities. The outlook is stable, S&P said in a statement.
Shopping centre operator Westfield Trust said it will acquire the Galleria shopping centre in Perth from joint vendors, retailer Coles Myer Ltd and life office Colonial Mutual, for A$289 million.

National Mutual Holdings Ltd delighted its big army of shareholders with a strong debut on Australian and New Zealand bourses on Tuesday and is expected to trade strongly on Wednesday. National Mutual shares closed A$1.80 or 20 percent above the level paid by retail investors and at a 13-percent premium to the price paid by institutional investors.
Vaccine and blood products manufacturer CSL Ltd said on Wednesday it had signed a joint venture agreement with Sweden's Astra AB to develop a vaccine to treat peptic ulcers and stomach cancers.
